description: Media Arts Year 5-6 width tiers — 5 standards, all capability strands. Generated from width_generation_prompt.md v1.0.
subject: Media Arts

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term — one media production task for a specific purpose or audience.
width_notes.typical_width: Full Y5-6 scope — multiple media forms and genres engaged, audience and purpose considerations applied, responsible media practice understood and applied.
width_notes.wider: Additional task contexts: different genres, platforms, purposes, technologies, First Nations Australian media arts contexts.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. First Nations elaborations always represented in wider.

AC9AMA6C01.minimum_width: Use media languages, technologies and production processes to construct one media arts work that communicates ideas or meaning for a specific, identifiable audience — making deliberate decisions about at least two production elements (framing, sound, editing, genre conventions).
AC9AMA6C01.typical_width: Construct media arts works across two or more forms or genres (advertisement, storyboarded film sequence, genre short film, game character design, music video section) for specific audiences; apply codes and conventions of established genres; use chroma key, special effects, editing and sound to enhance productions; reflect on production process using Viewpoints questions.
wider: Create a short genre film using chroma key, special effects, editing, sound effects and film language — applying genre conventions deliberately and reflecting on how each technical choice serves the audience relationship
Design a navigational plan for a game using multiple levels and obstacles — creating problems to solve before progressing, drawing on understanding of game genre conventions and player relationships
Create a music video section that brings together learning in music, dance and media arts — considering how the codes and conventions of music videos structure the audience experience
elaborations: producing a media arts work for a particular purpose; for example, creating an advertisement for a new toy or computer game
designing a storyboard that reflects a key scene in a sequence
designing and drawing a game character for a particular genre and considering the appropriate costume, mannerisms and typical dialogue
designing a navigational plan for a game using multiple levels and obstacles
considering the codes and conventions of music videos to create their own section of a music video
creating a short genre film using chroma key, special effects, editing, sound effects, film language and other technology
using Viewpoints to develop questions when reflecting on their production process

AC9AMA6D01.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one approach to manipulating media languages (framing, sound, editing, genre conventions) to communicate an idea or change meaning — and describe how the manipulation affects the audience experience.
AC9AMA6D01.typical_width: Develop production skills across multiple manipulation approaches — green screen/augmented reality to explore places, applying genre conventions to create humour or mood, using sound effects and music to change meaning, identifying story structures and technical elements that define genre; script and document a radio production including permission requirements.
wider: Trial applying conventions of an established genre to an everyday event to create humour (e.g. a visit to the library as an action movie) — experimenting with framing, music and sound effects, and reflecting on how genre conventions create audience expectation
Create a script for a radio production and document the permissions required for music and voice talent in a real-world community radio setting — practising professional media production workflows

Use augmented reality, virtual reality or chroma key to change an environment and convey new meaning — experimenting with multiple environment substitutions and comparing how each creates a different audience experience
elaborations: experimenting with approaches to capturing and sequencing images and text to create comic books, animations or stop motion videos that retell familiar stories
trialling options for applying the conventions of an established genre to an ordinary everyday event in order to create humour
using Viewpoints to develop questions when solving problems or making decisions about preferred options
identifying story structures and technical or symbolic elements that contribute to the formation of genre in media arts works
creating a script for a radio production and documenting the appropriate permissions that may be required for music and voice talents in a real-world community radio setting

AC9AMA6E01.minimum_width: Investigate at least one media arts work from a different time or cultural context and explain how context influences the characters, stories or values portrayed.
AC9AMA6E01.typical_width: Explore media arts works across different times and places; investigate how media languages and technologies are used to construct representations; examine stereotyping, bias and power relationships in media characters and stories; compare how context shapes values in media representations (e.g. family in TV across decades); discuss the role of media arts in sharing cultural information.
wider: Research and compare media representations of a topic (e.g. family, youth, heroes) created in different historical periods or countries — explaining how context shapes the characters, stories and values portrayed and how audiences might respond differently

Investigate how status and power relationships are constructed using framing, colour and costume (hero/villain creation) — applying findings to original character design that deliberately constructs or challenges a power relationship

Explore how media arts works share cultural information about people and their relationship with the environment — investigating examples from multiple cultural contexts and discussing what values are communicated
elaborations: investigating characters in games, considering issues such as stereotyping or bias
exploring status, such as power relationships, and showing different perspectives of character by using framing, colour and costume
using Viewpoints to develop questions that explore the impact of media technologies on the way the audience experiences a story
researching and comparing media representations created in different times and places
using Viewpoints to develop questions to explore new ideas
exploring how context influences the characters, stories and values portrayed in media arts works
discussing the role of media arts works in sharing cultural information about a group of people and their spirituality

AC9AMA6E02.minimum_width: Explore at least one First Nations Australian media arts work and explain how it contributes to sharing, maintaining, continuing or revitalising culture.
AC9AMA6E02.typical_width: Explore how and why First Nations Australian cultural expressions and media arts works are critical for sharing and revitalising cultures; investigate how cultural expressions change over time using community-published resources; examine how First Nations Australian media artists embed themselves and their communities in works as declarations of identity and visibility.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists represent their communities as superheroes or protagonists in comics, popular culture and television — examining how these representations function as visual declarations of identity, resilience and storytelling

Explore how cultural expressions created by First Nations Australian communities have changed over time by examining archived and contemporary media arts works — discussing what has been maintained and what has evolved

Using accredited First Nations Australian-published resources, investigate how and why cultural expressions are shared and maintained through media arts — discussing specific examples and what would be lost if these forms were not continued
elaborations: exploring (for example, by talking with First Nations Australians or accessing published resources accredited by First Nations Australian organisations) how and why cultural expressions and media arts works are critical for sharing, maintaining, continuing and revitalising cultures
identifying examples that illustrate how cultural expressions change over time

investigating the ways that First Nations Australian media artists embed themselves and their communities in media arts works in a range of representative forms as a visual declaration of identity, storytelling and resilience
using Viewpoints to develop questions that explore understandings about themes or issues in media arts works

AC9AMA6P01.minimum_width: Present a media arts work to an audience in at least one setting, applying at least one responsible media practice (e.g. online safety, cultural protocols, legal/ethical considerations).
AC9AMA6P01.typical_width: Present media arts works in informal and formal settings (classroom, school assembly, digital platforms); apply responsible media practices including legal, ethical and moral considerations and protocols for representing community or cultural stories; reflect on how different audiences receive and interpret the same work differently to intention.
wider: Present a short film to multiple audiences in different settings (classroom, school assembly, online platform) — reflecting systematically on how and why the work was received differently in each context and what this reveals about audience relationships

Present media arts works using internet-based technologies on curated digital platforms (school LMS), applying responsible media practice and online safety protocols, and engaging thoughtfully with audience responses

Investigate protocols for representing community or cultural stories in media arts works before creating and presenting a work — documenting the protocol decisions made and reflecting on how cultural understandings shaped the audience experience
elaborations: applying responsible media practices relating to the media arts works they are creating, such as legal, ethical and moral considerations
presenting a short film they have created to different audiences on different platforms
presenting their media arts works using internet-based media technologies
considering protocols for representing community or cultural stories in media arts works
reflecting on how and why understandings of culture were used within their media arts works, and their effect on the audience
